goal: A developer can start only from the public repository README, clone and configure a usable generic Claude Code/Codex environment on a supported platform, and verify that the published repository exposes no private knowledge, personal configuration, credentials, customer data, or conversation history.
persona: A developer familiar with a terminal who has Git and Python 3 installed, has not used this repository before, and does not have or supply Claude, Codex, GitHub, or other service credentials during the test.
public_entry: The rendered repository README at https://github.com/tasotaku/agent-lab-public; after opening it, the executor may follow only commands and links documented in that README.
test_data: Use a new temporary root for every journey and delete only that journey's temporary root after evidence has been retained.

Redirect HOME, USERPROFILE, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA, CODEX_HOME, Claude configuration locations documented by the README, Python caches, and global Git configuration to paths under the journey's temporary root before running repository commands.
Use no real credentials, tokens, private keys, customer records, personal knowledge files, normal Claude/Codex profiles, or pre-existing clone of the repository.

Record an action log containing each submitted command, exit code, monotonic start/end timestamps, working directory, relevant isolated environment-variable names and resolved paths, manual browser/terminal surface switches, and README scroll distance in viewport heights; redact environment values if any unexpected secret is encountered.

For content classification, an obviously synthetic placeholder such as example@example.com, YOUR_TOKEN, or a documented fake fixture is not private data; a realistic credential, person-specific or machine-specific setting, real customer record, exported conversation, or personal/business memory is prohibited.
Do not follow symlinks or delete paths that resolve outside the journey's temporary root; report any such path as a functional failure.
Windows is the immediate real-machine platform. macOS and Linux claims may be established by public isolated CI evidence for the exact tested commit.
minimal_test_count_rationale: Three independent journeys are the minimum because a real clean-profile install/use check, multi-OS evidence, and full public-surface privacy review require different environments and evidence types. Combining them would make failures state-dependent; splitting Windows install, check, and smoke use would add tests without adding risk coverage because those steps must share one installation state.

tests.title: README-only isolated Windows install and use
tests.user_task: Starting from the public README on a clean Windows machine, set up the generic environment, verify it, and exercise one credential-free reusable capability without touching your normal Claude or Codex configuration.
setup: Use a Windows machine with Git and Python 3 available and network access to the public GitHub repository; do not sign in to GitHub or any AI service.
Open the README URL in a fresh browser tab at 1366x768 with 100% zoom and the page at its top; open a fresh PowerShell terminal whose working directory is the empty isolated temporary root.

Before the first repository command, apply every isolation redirection listed in test_data and capture hashes plus recursive file inventories of the normal Claude/Codex profile locations (if they exist) for a before/after non-mutation comparison.
No repository files, commands, instructions, or prior test outcomes are known except what is visible from the public README.
actions: Read only the public README, find the Windows quick-start path, and submit its documented clone and install/configure commands exactly as shown except for substituting the isolated destination path where the README permits a path value.
From the resulting clone, run the README-documented check, doctor, or equivalent verification command.

Run one README-documented credential-free smoke or help operation that loads or exercises an installed reusable tool or skill; if the README offers several, choose the first one presented as the normal smoke path.

Compare the before/after inventories and hashes of normal Claude/Codex profiles, retain command output and the isolated installed-file inventory as evidence, then remove only the isolated temporary root.
functional_expectations: The public clone succeeds without authentication and the checked-out origin is https://github.com/tasotaku/agent-lab-public; record the tested commit SHA.
Every README-documented install/configure command used for the Windows path exits 0 without requesting credentials, access to a private repository, or input that the README did not explain.

The documented verification command exits 0 and explicitly reports present/valid results for generic rules, at least one reusable skill, reusable tooling, and both Claude Code and Codex configuration targets; a bare process-success message with no component results is insufficient.
The credential-free smoke/help operation exits 0 and identifies the installed capability from the isolated configured location, demonstrating that the result is consumable rather than merely copied.
All files created by clone/install/check/smoke resolve under the isolated temporary root, and the before/after inventories and hashes show no change to the machine's normal Claude/Codex profiles.

No command depends on files outside the fresh clone, Python standard environment, Git installation, or README-declared public dependencies; no broken symlink or symlink escaping the clone/config root is present.
Cleanup removes only the isolated temporary root and leaves the retained redacted evidence outside it.
ux_checks: From the initial 1366x768 README viewport through finding the Windows quick start, the executor needs at most 2 viewport-heights of downward scrolling; measure with the browser scroll position, and the visible heading or link must unambiguously distinguish Windows from macOS/Linux.

From an empty terminal to the first successful component verification, the normal Windows path requires at most 8 shell command submissions and 0 manual searches through repository files; count directly from the terminal action log, excluding the fixture's isolation setup and evidence-capture commands.

The README path requires at most 2 manual switches between the README browser tab and PowerShell from the first clone command through the smoke operation; count switches in the action log. Copying all commands once before execution is allowed.

Every command placeholder used by the normal path is explained adjacent to the command or in the immediately linked README section, and success/failure output names the next corrective action without requiring source inspection; record the first unexplained decision or opaque failure as a UX failure.

The successful verification output presents the component-level result before hashes, internal IDs, or diagnostic detail and is not reasonably confusable with a partial installation; assess the captured output and name the first misleading line if failed.
Judge whether the README and terminal flow are ready to ship unchanged to the stated developer persona, and report the single largest UX problem even when all numeric checks pass.
impossible_if: The public GitHub repository cannot be reached from the test machine before any repository response is received.
The Windows test host lacks working Git or Python 3 despite the fixture precondition and they cannot be restored without changing the fixture.
The test harness cannot redirect or observe the relevant profile paths, so non-mutation of normal profiles cannot be measured safely.
tests.isolation_requirements: Use a unique temporary root and isolated process environment for this journey. Do not read from, write to, launch with, or authenticate through normal Claude/Codex profiles. Capture normal-profile metadata only for non-mutation comparison, never its file contents. Resolve every cleanup target to an absolute descendant of the temporary root before deletion.

budget.basis: Up to eight documented shell submissions plus one README scan and one profile comparison should take about eight active minutes; public clone and dependency retrieval receive four additional minutes.

tests.title: Exact-commit cross-platform evidence
tests.user_task: Use the public README to confirm that the documented setup works in isolated Windows, macOS, and Linux environments for the same published revision, without relying on a maintainer's assertion.
setup: Open the public README in a fresh unsigned browser session at 1366x768 and 100% zoom.
Use a new isolated temporary root for any clone or downloaded public logs; do not use credentials or a pre-existing checkout.
The commit SHA under test is the SHA recorded by T1 if available; otherwise obtain it by the README-documented public clone path. T2 remains independent and does not reuse T1 files or session state.
actions: From the README, follow the documented compatibility/status link to the public automated evidence for the exact commit under test.

Inspect the run matrix and the logs or artifacts linked from each Windows, macOS, and Linux job; record runner OS/image, commit SHA, invoked public install command, isolation paths or clean-runner evidence, verification result, and completion state.
Compare the three jobs to the README's platform claims and documented commands, then remove only T2's isolated temporary root.
functional_expectations: The README publicly claims Windows, macOS, and Linux support and links directly to public automated compatibility evidence without requiring sign-in.

One completed successful job exists for each of Windows, macOS, and Linux on the exact tested commit SHA; a run from another commit, a skipped job, an allowed-failure job, or a job still in progress does not satisfy the expectation.

Each OS job starts from a clean hosted runner or equivalently documented isolated HOME/config/cache, uses the README-documented public installer path, runs the documented component verification, and reports valid generic rules, skill, tooling, Claude Code target, and Codex target.

The logs contain no use of repository, package, Claude, Codex, or cloud-service credentials other than GitHub's platform-provided read-only mechanics for checking out the same public repository; a job that depends on maintainer-only secrets fails.
The commands evidenced by CI do not contradict the README command for that OS, and platform-specific differences are explicitly documented in the README.
ux_checks: From the top of the rendered README, platform support and the link to exact-commit compatibility evidence are discoverable within 3 viewport-heights of scrolling at 1366x768; measure browser scroll position.

From selecting the README compatibility link to seeing the three-OS matrix requires at most 2 link activations and at most 1 manual browser-tab switch, with no site search or guessing a workflow name; count directly in the browser action log.

The matrix exposes OS name, pass/fail state, and commit identity before raw logs or internal job IDs, so a developer can distinguish full support from partial or stale evidence without opening more than one job per OS.
Judge whether the compatibility evidence is ready to ship unchanged to the stated developer persona, and report the single largest UX problem even when all numeric checks pass.
impossible_if: GitHub's public README or automation pages are unavailable before repository-specific content can be observed.
The public evidence provider suppresses all job status and logs for unsigned viewers, making commit, OS, and verification observations impossible.
tests.isolation_requirements: Use an unsigned browser session and a T2-only temporary root. Do not trigger privileged workflows, provide secrets, reuse T1's clone, or mutate the repository. Public read-only CI status, logs, and artifacts are the only acceptable cross-platform evidence.

budget.basis: README discovery and review of three already-completed public matrix jobs should take six active minutes, with two minutes allowed for public page/log retrieval.

tests.title: Public payload privacy and portability audit
tests.user_task: Starting only from the public README, audit everything the repository publishes and confirm that it contains reusable generic assets but no private, personal, credential, customer, or conversation material.
setup: Use a fresh isolated temporary root, unsigned public network access, and no prior clone, private source repository, private knowledge corpus, personal profile, or secret-detection allowlist.

Open the public README at 1366x768 and 100% zoom. The audit scope is all objects reachable from public branches and tags, commit messages, tracked files, submodule targets, symlink targets as paths, README-linked release assets, and README-linked setup artifacts; standard Git commit author fields and GitHub account/profile metadata are outside payload scope, but author-like data copied into file contents or commit messages is in scope.
Use the README-documented public audit/privacy command if present. Additional observation may classify its enumerated findings, but may not use commands or hidden allowlists absent from the README.
actions: Follow the README's documented privacy/audit path to obtain a full public clone or audit artifact and record the exact commit plus every public ref included in the scan.
Run the README-documented audit command and retain its machine-readable or line-addressable results, including scanner identity/version, enumerated scope, exclusions, and findings.

Review every non-vendored text finding and all audit-listed high-entropy, credential-pattern, absolute-path, identity, customer-record, conversation/transcript, knowledge/memory, symlink, submodule, and release-asset findings against the prohibited-category definitions in test_data.

Confirm from the audited inventory that the public payload actually includes generic rules, reusable skills, reusable tooling, installer code, and documentation rather than passing privacy checks as an empty shell; then remove only T3's isolated temporary root.
functional_expectations: The README documents a reproducible public privacy/audit command that exits 0 on the tested revision and enumerates all public branches/tags and README-linked release/setup artifacts; an audit limited silently to the default working tree is insufficient.

Credential scanning reports zero verified secrets, tokens, passwords, private keys, credential-bearing URLs, or realistic high-entropy credentials across the full scope. Synthetic placeholders are acceptable only when visibly marked fake and unusable.

Content/path review finds zero personal configuration payloads: no real absolute user-home paths, usernames, personal email addresses in payload content, machine hostnames, normal-profile copies, editor/session state, or settings tied to one person's accounts or filesystem.

Content review finds zero private knowledge or customer data: no personal/business memory notes, private project facts, customer names joined with contact/account/ticket/content records, internal-only datasets, or instructions whose usefulness depends on undisclosed private context.

Content review finds zero conversation history: no exported chats, prompt/response transcripts, tool-call logs, session summaries, or conversation databases; clearly fictional minimal snippets used to explain a generic format are acceptable only when labeled as examples and contain no real identity or context.

Every submodule URL and README-linked dependency/artifact required by install is publicly readable without credentials; every symlink resolves within its intended public clone/config tree and does not expose a local or private path.

The audited inventory includes substantive generic rules, at least one reusable skill, reusable tooling, a cross-platform installer, and public setup/verification documentation, and the audit reports no ignored or unclassified non-vendored payload.

Commit messages in public history contain none of the prohibited categories and no reference to a private filesystem path, private repository URL, credential, customer record, or pasted conversation content.
ux_checks: From the top of the rendered README, the privacy/publication guarantee and reproducible audit command are discoverable within 3 viewport-heights of scrolling at 1366x768; measure browser scroll position.

From a completed public clone to a final audit verdict requires at most 3 documented shell command submissions and no manual search for hidden scripts, exclusions, or allowlists; count commands from the terminal action log, excluding fixture setup and evidence capture.

The final audit summary leads with the five prohibited-category verdicts and scanned-scope counts before hashes or raw diagnostic detail, and any exclusion names the excluded path, reason, and risk; assess the captured output rather than inferring from exit code alone.

A developer can map every finding to a public ref and file/artifact plus line or object identifier without reading audit implementation source; any unlocatable warning is a UX failure even if the overall command exits 0.
Judge whether the privacy/audit flow is ready to ship unchanged to the stated developer persona, and report the single largest UX problem even when all numeric checks pass.
impossible_if: The public repository cannot be cloned and its public refs cannot be enumerated because GitHub is unavailable before repository-specific data is returned.
A README-linked public release/setup artifact has been removed by its host and no immutable copy or digest-addressed substitute is available, preventing complete payload observation.
The documented audit requires private credentials or access to non-public source; report impossible rather than supplying those credentials.
tests.isolation_requirements: Use only T3's temporary root, public unsigned access, and README-documented commands. Never compare with or read the private agent-lab repository, personal profiles, private knowledge, credentials, customer data, or prior conversation exports. Resolve cleanup paths before deletion and retain only redacted audit evidence.

budget.basis: A documented full-ref scan plus manual classification of surfaced findings and inventory completeness is expected to take twelve active minutes; cloning refs and fetching public scan metadata receive three minutes.

covered_risks: README-only discoverability and reproducibility on an immediate Windows machine
Isolation from normal Claude/Codex profiles and credential-free operation
Presence and consumability of generic rules, reusable skills, tooling, and both configuration targets
Cross-platform installer claims for Windows, macOS, and Linux at the exact commit
Secrets and credentials across public refs, history, and linked artifacts
Personal configuration and machine-specific path leakage
Private knowledge, customer data, and conversation-history leakage
Private dependencies, escaping symlinks, stale evidence, and empty-shell publication
README and CLI discovery cost, decision ambiguity, and audit-result readability
blind_spots: T2 validates macOS and Linux through isolated public CI evidence rather than hands-on use on physical macOS/Linux machines.
No credentialed end-to-end Claude Code or Codex model invocation is performed, so account login, paid API access, and live model behavior are not covered.

A context-free public-payload review can detect material that is intrinsically personal or customer-specific, but cannot prove that innocuous-looking text was derived from an undisclosed private source without an external provenance oracle.
Objects deleted from all public refs before the test and external pages not linked by the README are not observable as current public repository contents.
